approach: Decide a shared cause by where the failure arose, not by what its text says. In crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, `ItemEnd::Failed` carries a `Failure { reason, shared: Option<String> }`, built in `attempts` from the last failed attempt. `shared` is Some(normalized detail) only for failures that do not come from a verdict on the item: (a) a run that ended with no outcome (`Run.outcome == None`, the Err path of `RealSteps::run`, drain.rs ~3562, and not held or needs-accepting), (b) a read that returned no job and an error (`RealSteps::read` Err arm, ~3510), and (c) a landing that did not land (`Landing::NotLanded` or the failed re-check after a rebase), using its detail. Any run that finished with an outcome (Rejected, Failed, TimedOut, including the critic's reject, the planning cap, the verifier and scope-guard verdicts) is `shared: None`, so it is never shared. `Drain::finish` runs one lock section. If the item has `shared: Some(key)` and an earlier DIFFERENT item recorded the same key in a new `State.failures`, it calls `set_stop(Stop::RepeatedFailure, Some(item))` with a note naming both items. Otherwise it records the key, adds a note, and calls `pass_over`, so the worker takes the next item exactly as for Paused and Skipped. Environment stops are untouched. Tests get a scriptable per-run result on `Stub` and `Shared`, and a scriptable landing detail on `Stub`, so a real shared cause can be set up without putting classification in the double. Docs, display and CHANGELOG are updated. Files outside the listed deliverables (main.rs help, README, docs/design, docs/decisions.md, docs/spec.toml) are not touched.

decisions.choice: Classify the cause where the failure is made: add `Failure { reason: String, shared: Option<String> }` and carry it in `RunStep::Failed { failure }` and `ItemEnd::Failed(Failure)`. `run_job` sets `shared` when `run.outcome.is_none()` in the `other` arm (1561-1574) and when the read returned no job with an error (1504). `attempts` sets it for `LandStep::NotLanded` from `st.jobs[at].landing` (written at 1650 and 1698). `attempts` returns the last attempt's failure at `failures >= ATTEMPTS`.
decisions.reason: Drain::run (3543-3577) and the planner/critic paths produce fixed sentences for verdicts on one item (for example 'the critic rejected the plan', PLANNING_CAP_REASON). Comparing text would stop the batch for two unrelated verdicts, which is the reported fault. `Run.outcome` already separates a finished verdict (Some) from an Athena or host error (None; its doc at 392 says 'None when the job did not reach an outcome'). This needs no new field on `Run` and no change to the `Steps` trait or any impl. It answers findings 5 and 7: the cause kind is known in `attempts` and `finish` receives it.

decisions.choice: Treat a finished outcome of any kind (Rejected, Failed, TimedOut) as a verdict on the item, never shared.
decisions.reason: The request names the shared causes as the environment, the build and Athena itself. A finished run does not say which of those it was, and the text cannot tell. Pausing the item is the safe default; the cost of a miss is one more paused item with a visible note, bounded by budget and job limit.

rejected.why: A producer that crashes on its own task is a Failed outcome too; that is per item.

decisions.choice: Compare keys only between shared failures: `State.failures: Vec<(String item, String key)>` holds shared keys only. The key is the detail lower-cased and split on whitespace, with edge punctuation trimmed. A token equal to the item's name or the retry job's name, a job-id-shaped token (`dddddddd-dddddd-xxxx`), or an all-digit token (pull request numbers) becomes a placeholder. The tokens are re-joined with single spaces. An empty result is `None` and never matches.
decisions.reason: A landing or host error often embeds the job name or a PR number, which would make an identical cause look different. Whole-token matching avoids corrupting short names such as `a`. Check-and-insert share one `self.st()` lock section, so two concurrent workers (`drain_concurrent`) cannot both miss each other.

risks.risk: Two unrelated verdicts with the same fixed sentence (critic reject, planning cap) are taken as a shared cause.
risks.mitigation: Only failures without an outcome (Err path of run or read) and landing failures can be shared, and the key must match after masking. A rejection, timeout or Failed outcome is never shared. A unit test shows two items with 'the critic rejected the plan' do not match, and criterion 2 case (3) and criterion 3 case (1) run it through the drain.

risks.risk: A true shared cause is missed because its text embeds per-item data (paths, counts), so the batch pauses items one at a time.
risks.mitigation: Masking handles the item and retry job names, job ids and numbers, and the comparison is on the whole normalized detail. A miss only pauses more items, each with a visible note; the budget and job limit bound the run. The unit tests pin realistic landing details.

risks.risk: The tests could rely on the stub's own text rather than on the production classification.
risks.mitigation: The classification lives in production code, and the doubles return scripted `Run`/`Landing` values only. A control case with a verdict reason must continue, so the test cannot pass by relying on matching text.

risks.risk: The Before::RepeatedFailure seeding runs through two workers with timing waits, and a second failing item changes the order.
risks.mitigation: Rework the seeding with `errors: ["bad","bad2"]` and `wait_for ('new','end bad2-retry')`; the `wait_for` loop already waits for the entry and then 150 ms for the stop to be stored. Keep the asserted row counts and run the whole file before finishing.

risks.risk: A failed item stays in report.queued and the next `athena drain` retries it, so a permanently failing item repeats across runs.
risks.mitigation: Matches how Paused and Skipped items behave; the note says 'paused for this run'. A persistent pause would touch the scope guard, which is out of scope.

risks.risk: Adding a field to `RunStep::Failed` and a payload to `ItemEnd::Failed` breaks other matches in drain.rs.
risks.mitigation: The compiler flags every missed construction; the field is added in step 3 before the callers change. The existing `Stub` and `Shared` default to the old behavior when the new fields are empty.

open_questions: User: Four texts say a repeated failure stops the drain for one item and become stale: the `athena drain --help` stop list (crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs:254), README.md:126, docs/design/async-drain.md:179 and docs/spec.toml:1351. User: A finished run with outcome Failed or TimedOut is treated as a verdict on the item, so two such items never stop the batch. A shared build or environment fault that shows up as a Failed outcome (not an Err) would pause items one by one until budget or job limit. Is that the wanted trade-off, or should a Failed outcome count as shared?
